text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 3123459999 - kv-cache fragmentation & continuous-batching regression detected in prod-east-1. P95 latency spike >= 4x, pod OOMs observed. Auto-pager triggered.

maria: acked. i’m oncall for prod-east. switching to incident channel. pulling metrics now.

sam: seeing huge kv_arena.free_list growth and repeated cuda malloc failures in logs. suspect fragmentation after last cont-batching rollout.

leo: reported customer error rates up ~6% for embedding endpoints (retries spiking). correlated with higher batch sizes around 512 tokens.

carla: paging history shows a gradual increase starting ~3123457000 then sharp at 3123459800. cfg change: cont-batch policy rolled at 3123456000 (auto-burst enabled).

dinesh: can we quickly flip the batch policy back to conservative? i can push a hotfix to runtime flags to cap batch size and disable burst.

maria: yes. priority: prevent more OOMs and reduce latency. plan: 1) disable cont-batch burst, 2) apply arena compaction & reduce max_chunk, 3) restart affected inference pods with PT_MALLOC flags, 4) monitor.

oncall-bot: @maria, @dinesh, @sam assigned. ETA 15m for mitigation window.

sam: patch ready. hotfix diff: 
```yaml
# runtime flags patch
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 256  # down from 1024
  burst_enabled: false
  max_batch_items: 32
```
apply with: `kubectl apply -f contbatch-hotfix.yaml --namespace=prod-east`

carla: note - need to coordinate with rollout bot to avoid simultaneous restarts across all racks. prefer canary across rack-a then ramp.

maria: agree. canary 3 pods in rack-a, wait 2min, then ramp to remaining. executing now.

sam: canary applied to rack-a. logs show reduced long-tail batch assembly times. no new OOMs in canary.

leo: running arena compaction script on canary pods: 
```bash
# compact arenas to reduce fragmentation
python tools/kv_arena_compact.py --target /dev/gpumem --force --grace-period=5
```
compaction started.

dinesh: also toggling environment to `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.8,max_split_size_mb:16` on canary restart to reduce fragmentation.

maria: canary looks stable for 7 minutes. p95 dropped back to ~normal. expanding to rack-b now.

oncall-bot: rolling hotfix to rack-b/rack-c. ETA full rollout 12m.

carla: customer impact: we’ve seen ~18 customers with transient 5xx retries, top affected are search-api-prod and embeddings-batch. SRE oncall notified accounts team.

leo: posted alert to status page draft. marking as partial-degradation.

sam: during rollouts, one older GPU node still shows repeated `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` lines; killing and recreating pod solved it. flagging as potential stale driver state.

dinesh: opened internal ticket to coordinate node-driver rotation; not blocking current mitigation.

maria: full rollout done. p95 back to baseline. KV arena free_list reduced by ~70% after compaction and restart. no further OOMs in last 10m.

carla: compiling timeline and customer impact summary for postmortem. initial severity: Sev2 -> re-evaluate after 24h.

leo: actions for postmortem: 
- revert cont-batching burst logic until we validate fragmentation under load
- add arena compaction to autoscaled maintenance windows
- add telemetry for per-model batch size distribution and per-arena fragmentation ratio
- harden node driver rotation playbook

maria: temporary mitigations remain: cont-batch caps and PT_MALLOC env tweaks. leaving mitigation in place for 48h while we run soak tests.

dinesh: will run a load replay on staging to reproduce fragmentation with current batching policy and test quantized kernels.

oncall-bot: incident 3123459999 -> status: mitigation applied. next update in 30m or on any regression.

sam: thanks team. adding logs snippet for postmortem: 
```
[3123459712] kv_arena.cpp:543 WARN free_list_size=128912 frag_ratio=0.93
[3123459750] runtime.cpp:201 ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (code 2)
[3123459782] batcher.cpp:89 WARN assembled_batch_tokens=980 queued=24
```

maria: leaving this channel open. if we see new OOMs escalate pager and follow incident runbook. :white_check_mark:
